items.title: Was Benjamin Franklin the original wellness bro? I lived like him for a day to find out
items.standfirst: Before online influencers existed, the founding father published an annual wellness pamphlet. I followed his 13 virtues he found necessary for a good lifeBenjamin Franklin doesn’t get enough credit. Yes, he was a founding father of the United States; he invented the lightning rod and his face is printed on $100 bills. But rarely is he celebrated for his contributions to the most meaningful field of human achievement: wellness influencing.Centuries before GRWM videos and scientifically dubious podcasts were a dollar-sign-shaped glint in their creators’ eyes, Franklin was doling out life advice. Under the pseudonym Poor Richard, Franklin published an annual pamphlet and minted maxims like “Diligence is the mother of good luck” and “Fish and visitors stink after three days.” Continue reading...

items.title: Soaring popularity of pickleball linked to eye injuries and disease, doctors warn
items.standfirst: Woman hit in eye developed glaucoma as a result, with other injuries including retinal tearsDoctors have issued a warning about eye injuries linked to the rapid rise in popularity of pickleball, after a woman in her early 50s who was hit in the eye during a game developed glaucoma.She sustained a direct hit to her left eye while playing without protective eyewear. The woman reported immediate blurry vision, severe pain and extreme light sensitivity. After emergency treatment, she was discharged from hospital and her symptoms seemed to be resolving.
